content:
Wow, I'm genuinely impressed. Samsung had a seven-year head start in the foldable market, and Apple held off until it could do it better than anyone else — and the iPhone Duo actually delivers!

It's clear Apple has given serious thought to what a foldable iPhone should be, and has truly maximised every advantage of this form factor...

First, the fundamentals. As previous reports have mentioned, Apple waited until it could make the crease nearly invisible, ensuring the hinge is durable enough to withstand countless open and close cycles. The hinge's durability remains to be seen, but the effort they've put into the hinge design is already apparent.

Then there's the under-display front camera — visible when you need it, virtually invisible when you don't.

Apple has also considered different ways of holding and positioning the device, then worked out how software can make the most of this form factor.

I can't remember who said it first, but I think this quote is spot on: great design is something others can't imagine, but in hindsight feels completely obvious. The original iPhone was a perfect example. Other smartphones came with physical keyboards and required a stylus to use, but the iPhone worked with just your fingers, and the keyboard only appeared when needed. In hindsight, of course that's how a smartphone should work.

*Yes, the Duo supports Apple Pencil, but doesn't require one.

For me, the Duo presentation had plenty of moments like that. Why do we have to select a subject in a photo first, then copy it into another app, instead of just dragging it directly from the original image? Seems obvious in hindsight.

Swapping the selfie timer for the device automatically waiting until everyone has stopped moving before taking the shot. So obvious!

Top Liked Comment by Jordan

I think Apple's marketing and visual design are always top-notch. My first reaction is usually: wow, that looks amazing, I want that. But then reality kicks in — especially with this device. The 2k pricing makes the decision much easier, and given the tight supply, I expect to be waiting until early 2027 for stock... Prices have gone up across the board, even on refurbished units. It's a broader trend, but it really takes the shine off things. I used to always tell people to treat buying a phone like buying a car — pick one and invest in it for years. That advice feels even more relevant now, because phones will eventually cost as much as a car!

Some UI features are actually pointless, but they look great — like the blur effect when folding the device.

I could go on for ages, but to sum up: my expectations for this device were already sky-high, and it still managed to exceed them by a mile. I'm British, and we usually use "wow" sarcastically — but I used that word at the start of this article with absolutely zero irony.

This isn't the right device for me personally. For me, an iPhone is roughly 50% ultra-thin camera, 49% pocket computer, 1% phone. The iPhone 18 Pro Max is much more my speed. But I have an intense craving for the iPhone Duo.

Which brings me to what the headline calls "the worst thing about Apple." Apple knows how to make product videos that make you feel like you could reach through the screen and touch the device. Apple can make you desperately want a product you have absolutely no business buying. I'm not the target audience for the iPhone Duo, but I genuinely, absolutely, unequivocally want to buy one. What about you?
